body: We don't add trailing slashes to any other paths, why is this special?
@markstory afaik all paths have the trailing slash except for ROOT which is somewhat special. I wonder why this one above dont then.

@davidsteinsland It would be cleaner if CakePHP didn't have to check on that because they would always be trailing in the first place. Personally, I would rather find the root cause of this issue and fix it there.

@dereuromark What I meant was that all the user supplied paths don't get trailing slashes added to them either.

@davidsteinsland The framework expects that you put paths in correctly. I'm sure we could go around fixing paths, but I'm not sure the overhead is worth it when the solution is documented.
@markstory Now I understand. Yeah, the user needs to take care of that.

It should be clearly documented then, because I did not figure this thing out until I realized the plugin wasn't loaded.

There isn't a big difference in writing the path with/without a trailing slash, but when one of them leads to an error it's kinda confusing.

I agree.
Alternatively in debug mode it could check on a slash present and if not throw an exception.
Why? Documentation solves the problem I think.
@davidsteinsland Can you maybe make a docs PR with the suggested note?

I also just had the case that somewhere someone included App::build() additions with hardcoded / which lead to problems along the way on WIN os, for example.
But I think this could be solvable as user-land-implementation (exception when invalid paths are detected) that only takes effect in debug mode (similar to DebugKit), so there is probably no need to act other than documentation.
